description: Synthetic fixture for the stub-transport endpoint tests (tests/test_endpoint.py, tests/test_agent_loop.py). It is NOT ground truth for any real clip and is not read by eval/run_eval.py.

object_matching.description: Predicted object tracks are matched to ground-truth object tracks by class_label and temporal IoU of [first_seen_s, last_seen_s] with tolerance set in eval/run_eval.py. max_count is a track-level advisory field indicating the maximum number of instances of that class observed on-screen simultaneously during the track; it is not used in the default matching metric but is available for alternative metrics.

event_track_association.description: Each presence:* event row corresponds to exactly one ground-truth object track. For example, the presence:person event with interval 3.0–55.0 is the event emitted by gt_track_1, and the presence:person event with interval 18.0–47.0 is the event emitted by gt_track_2. The evaluator matches predicted events to ground-truth events by event_type and temporal overlap, respecting that multiple events of the same type may exist from different tracks (issue #126).

counts_independence.description: The counts table provides per-minute summary statistics (maximum distinct track count per class_label) and is evaluated independently of the events table. Conflicts between counts and events are avoided because counts measure distinct track presence per minute window regardless of exact start/end times, while events carry exact intervals per track. Precision/recall for counts is computed separately (issue #125).

notes: Ground-truth times are offsets in seconds from clip start. Count semantics: 'count' is the number of distinct ground-truth tracks of that class_label observed in that minute (max unique track count across the minute window). Track IDs are opaque identifiers used only to associate objects with their ground truth tracks.
